fields.title: The author workspace
fields.subtitle: Write, move a chapter, count, export

beats.say: An author opens a book, writes in a chapter, and exports the whole book. This is the second acceptance script for Open Editor.

fields.title: A book is a manifest and its chapters
fields.body: book.json  ·  one file for each chapter  ·  an id that never changes

beats.say: A book is one small file that lists the chapters in order, and one file for each chapter. Every chapter has an id that never changes.
Here is a short example book. Three chapters, and the word count for the book.
Choose a chapter. It opens with its heading, its list and its footnote.
Write, and the count follows. The chapter is marked as unsaved.
beats.label: the count follows every _word_

beats.say: The arrows move a chapter. This one goes to the end of the book. Its id stays the same.
beats.label: a move changes the *order*, nothing else

beats.say: Save writes only what changed: one chapter, and the order.
beats.label: written only on *save*

beats.say: Export gives the whole book in one file, in the new order. Here it is as Markdown.
beats.text: Export gives the whole book in one file, in the new order. Here it is as Markdown.
beats.label: the whole book, _one file_

fields.title: What the editor writes is always a valid book

beats.say: A test plays these steps on every change, in three browsers. It checks every saved file against the format, and that an untouched chapter stays exactly as it was.
An author cannot add a footnote or an image yet. Both audiences now have a working script. Measuring the engines comes next.
